arm64FixtureCrossLink.scope: Only changed freestanding fixture assembly and atomic operations were cross-linked with a cached compiler; this is not ARM service/kernel runtime proof.

sharedCoreBuild.scope: Current shared production core rebuilt serially; no new full GUI/CLI/Lua runtime proof claimed.

proof: The original leader actually exits; separate CPU-loop and console siblings use separate stacks. The service demonstrably selects the intended nonleader and retains a completed real mmap after a detach error.

Only test-linked hooks operate the fixture flag and resume the actual restored selected task. The application executes its own thread-only exit; WNOWAIT leaves its actual exit(0) notification for the service owner.

The completed original allocation is recorded before transient retry and remains owned after confirmed task death. The stale task-context query no longer rejects a live original mm before the guarded handoff.
Fresh private mapping alias proof authorizes the surviving member cleanup using the original pinned descriptor, never old GP replay or source numeric TID reopening.
Independent before/after kernel snapshots compare every survivor GP/extended register and mask bit. Independent pinned-mm reads and maps require allocation absence while the original mm still lives.

Recovery after recording, death during the first transient retry before caller return, and service destruction all reclaim their actual old allocation, preserve code/console liveness and reap the original process normally.
proofLimits: Both new live profiles are native x86-64 and i386 on the recorded host kernel, using borrowed Unix syscall sites and a restored-context detach failure.
No new claim for mixed entry ABI handoff, x32, ARM, Wine, other kernels or full GUI/CLI/Lua routing.

Automatic discovery/ownership of a separate old-mm process, concurrent/nonleader exec, earlier death phases, ambiguous ESRCH while running, cancellation and policy/read-only transports still need implementation/live proof.
New service failure cases do not provide dedicated failed current-proof cleanup/dual-guard or general native-call frame ownership proofs.
